fact: The mortal Twin — a single point to the eye that is really six stars bound together.
bio: Castor (Alpha Geminorum) lies about 51 light-years away and is one of the most remarkable multiple systems in the sky: three pairs of stars — two bright white A-type stars, each with a red-dwarf companion, plus a distant red-dwarf pair — all gravitationally bound, six suns in one 'star'.
cultural: Castor is the mortal horseman of the Dioscuri, twin brother of Pollux in Greek and Roman myth. Though labelled 'Alpha', it is usually slightly fainter than its brother Pollux beside it.
